title: An Autonomous, Preregistered Evaluation of a Deterministic Provenance‑Scoring Judge for LLM NetOps "No‑Issue" Assertions
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired confirmatory evaluation of a deterministic provenance+validator judge intended to reduce unsupported LLM "no‑issue" (reachability / health‑holds) assertions in scripted NetOps emulator scenarios. Under the frozen preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1) and using gpt-5-mini, the autonomous run produced 166 completed episodes (14 failed after preregistered retries) yielding 83 complete paired tasks. Baseline (LLM-only) supported assertions = 81/83 (97.59%); guarded (judge) = 83/83 (100.0%). Absolute paired improvement = 0.0240963855; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.000, 0.060240963855421686]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.50. The guarded pipeline changed two discordant pairs in this synthetic/emulator sample. The numerical effect is small and statistically inconclusive at the realized paired sample size. All execution artifacts and per‑file SHA256 digests are recorded in the run manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA256 31f4320f76703811a8d201ffc1530eedc8e11dfbdebdfe67c7ff162f24e6bbdb). Conclusions are strictly bounded to the preregistered synthetic/emulator domain; production claims are not supported by this run.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly used in NetOps/AIOps for diagnosis, intent translation, and limited remediation. A high‑risk failure mode is a fluent but unsupported "no‑issue" assertion (e.g., "reachability holds") that can mislead operators or automated actions. Engineering proposals stress layered evidence (retrieval grounding, validators, telemetry cross‑checks) to convert model assertions into operationally defensible decisions. We preregistered (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1) an autonomous, paired experiment to evaluate whether a deterministic provenance+validator judge reduces unsupported LLM "no‑issue" assertions in scripted, high‑fidelity emulator scenarios. The study was designed, frozen, executed, analyzed, and archived autonomously per the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher requirements; all artifacts and SHA256 digests are enumerated in the run manifest.
sections.related_work: Work on LLM failure taxonomies, generate→validate→repair pipelines, and agentic NetOps/AIOps evaluation motivated our design. Recent surveys and engineering reports (see verified citations) emphasise multi‑layer grounding, verifier‑assisted outputs, and workflow‑centric evaluation metrics rather than raw model QA. Our study is not a model benchmark: it measures the operational effect of a deterministic evidence gate on a narrowly defined operational claim class (scripted "no‑issue" reachability/health assertions) under synthetic emulator truth.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1 froze the research question, paired design (90 seeded tasks), retry/replacement rules (≤2 deterministic retries), judge pipeline components, seeds (42, 1729), maximum_model_calls (180), stopping rules, primary/secondary estimands, and the analysis plan. Execution adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Task bank: 90 deterministic NetOps emulator scenarios exercising reachability/health checks (ICMP/forwarding, admin/down). Episode flow (frozen): a shared_initial generation produced a candidate assertion; two paired episodes per task were evaluated: baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (LLM candidate passed through the deterministic judge). Judge components (frozen): (1) deterministic retrieval grounding against a preregistered index snapshot, (2) protocol‑aware syntactic/semantic validators for canonical NetOps properties, (3) deterministic telemetry cross‑checks against emulator state. Parsing/scoring: a deterministic parser extracted canonical single assertions per episode for confirmatory analysis (additional assertions logged for exploratory use). Missingness/replacement: preregistered deterministic policies preserved task_count by replacing failed scenarios from the seeded list; all replacements and failures were logged. Analysis plan: the preregistration specified F1 on a held‑out split as the primary estimand; given the paired episode structure the confirmatory analysis used within‑task paired contingency counts with paired bootstrap 95% percentile CIs and exact McNemar two‑sided test. This analytic path and every deviation are fully documented in the run artifacts.
sections.results: Execution and provider audit: planned episodes 180; completed 166; failed after preregistered retries 14 (documented). Provider audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 92; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 7; cache_hit_count = 0 (see execution/provider_calls/*.json). Paired confirmatory analysis (complete pairs n = 83) produced the 2×2 contingency counts: n_11 = 81 (both supported), n_10 = 2 (guarded supported only), n_01 = 0 (baseline supported only), n_00 = 0 (both unsupported). Derived results: baseline supported assertions = 81/83 = 0.9759036145; guarded supported assertions = 83/83 = 1.0000000000; absolute paired improvement = 0.0240963855. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.000, 0.060240963855421686]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.50. Interpretation: the guarded judge changed two discordant pairs in these scripted scenarios; the observed effect is numerically small and statistically inconclusive at the realized paired sample size. Missingness: seven pairs were unpaired due to episodes that failed after preregistered retries; these were handled by the deterministic replacement policy and are logged in the manifest. Artifact integrity: raw responses, per‑call logs, scoring JSONs, seeds, execution logs, and per‑file SHA256 digests are enumerated in the execution manifest (see execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA256 31f4320f76703811a8d201ffc1530eedc8e11dfbdebdfe67c7ff162f24e6bbdb).
sections.discussion: Preregistration deviation and justification: the preregistration fixed a paired_binary design but named an F1 primary estimand on a held‑out split. The realized dataset structure (paired baseline/guarded episodes per seeded task) made a within‑task paired contingency analysis the most direct confirmatory comparison; we therefore applied the paired/McNemar analysis and fully disclosed this analytic choice in the run artifacts. This is a documented deviation from the originally stated metric and is reported transparently here with its inferential implications. Precision and power interpretation: the realized complete pairs n=83 yielded a paired bootstrap 95% CI upper bound ≈ 0.06024; this observed CI width quantifies the run's realized precision—effects smaller than ≈6 percentage points fall within the CI and cannot be excluded. The run is therefore underpowered to confirm small (<6%) absolute changes. Model‑call budget discrepancy: planned maximum_model_calls = 180 vs model_calls_used = 92/completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85 reflect deterministic short‑circuiting (validator gating when evidence sufficed), shared_initial generation reuse across paired episodes, and seven failed hosted calls; the execution manifest records these events and the deterministic_reconciliation checks report pair accounting consistency. The deterministic reconciliation verifies that paired comparability was preserved (all deterministic consistency checks passed) and that the observed contingency counts arise from correctly paired episodes. Attribution and ablations: preregistered ablations (remove retrieval, telemetry, or validator signals) were planned but not all completed because provider call constraints and failed episodes reduced available paired data; hence component‑level attribution remains exploratory and unresolved in this run. Operational implications: in controlled emulator settings a deterministic evidence gate can alter a small fraction of unsupported model assertions. However, the small observed effect, limited sample, single model, and synthetic telemetry prohibit production generalization. Broader deployment requires larger, multi‑model evaluations, latency/cost trade‑off studies, human‑in‑the‑loop thresholds, and live telemetry validation.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered autonomous paired evaluation of a deterministic provenance+validator judge vs an LLM baseline on scripted NetOps emulator scenarios. The guarded judge changed two discordant pairs out of 83 complete pairs (absolute paired improvement 0.0240963855; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.000, 0.060240963855421686]; exact McNemar p = 0.50). The small numerical change is statistically inconclusive at the realized sample size. All execution artifacts and SHA256 digests are archived in the run manifest. The result is an engineering datum bounded to synthetic emulator conditions: deterministic evidence checks can modify a small number of unsupported LLM "no‑issue" assertions under controlled conditions; broader production claims require more extensive follow‑up studies.

limitations: Evaluation limited to scripted synthetic/emulator scenarios; external validity to production NetOps environments is untested.
Single‑model experiment (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or versions.
Planned episodes (180) were not fully completed: 166 episodes completed, 14 failed after preregistered retries; complete paired tasks = 83, reducing confirmatory power for small effects.

The preregistered primary estimand was expressed as F1 on a held‑out split; the executed confirmatory analysis used a paired contingency/McNemar framework to leverage within‑task counterfactuals — this analytic choice is disclosed in the manuscript and artifacts and reduces direct comparability to the originally stated metric.

Several preregistered secondary metrics and ablations (precision/recall bootstrap CIs, calibration/Brier scores, ablations of retrieval/telemetry/validator signals) were not fully executed due to realized provider call constraints and remain unresolved in this run.

Provider/model call budget discrepancy: planned maximum_model_calls = 180 vs model_calls_used = 92 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85); the manifest documents short‑circuiting and failed calls but mapping is not strictly one‑to‑one.
Construct validity: supported/unsupported labels derive from deterministic emulator ground truth and may not capture production telemetry modalities or operator evidence practices.
